svg.title: Rung 9's learning test with the slow Kenyon cell current: MBON11's responses before and after pairing each odor
svg.text: Rung 9's learning test with the slow Kenyon cell current
With the Kenyon cell current as slow as flies' flash EPSC, MBON11's response to 3-octanol holds: 51 spikes/s from 0.5 s to the odor's end (before 12; flies 95-100),
71 evoked spikes (before 39; flies 118), 34% of them in the first 0.3 s (before 79%). Pairing 3-octanol cuts its response 90% (flies 80%) and 4-methylcyclohexanol's
42% (flies 27%); pairing 4-methylcyclohexanol cuts its own 95% (flies 76%) but 3-octanol's only 9% (flies 38%): its Kenyon cells are still too few.

svg.text: flies before pairing (Hige et al. 2015, read off Fig. 1E)
before, with the old 5 ms current
The model: mean of 4 seeds of 8 flies, smoothed as Hige et al. smoothed theirs (a Gaussian, SD 50 ms, which also spreads each rise earlier). Evoked spikes: 0-1.4 s, above the rest.
